A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UEFL and retain matching methods and experiments. All 16 pages of v3 and 18 pages of v4, including appendices A–D and A–L respectively, support text and visual comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original UEFL experiments on heterogeneous image classification, domain generalization, and label heterogeneity, together with codebook and client-imbalance ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds 100-client evaluations, heterogeneity controls, uncertainty-estimator comparisons, neural-collapse experiments, and convergence curves.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the encoder–discretizer–classifier pipeline, K-means extensions, segmentation, losses, and entropy trigger. V4's aggregation explanation and five-iteration limit provide implementation information without establishing an underlying method revision; the codebook-size notation changes from n to v.

E1.justification: V4 adds EMNIST-L in Table 4 and unrotated/lower-severity and varying-rotation CIFAR100 scenarios in Appendix C. This modestly extends image-classification coverage; the original datasets, domain-generalization tasks, and label-heterogeneity evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Existing comparator sets are retained in their corresponding experiments. V4 adds FedCR to the new 100-client comparison, zero-error and neural-collapse controls in Table 10, and a Deep Ensemble alternative in Table 9. FedIIR remains in the original domain-generalization and 50-client comparisons.

E3.justification: V4 adds substantial experimental designs: 100-client evaluation; five-client CIFAR100 tests with 10,000 images per client and scratch/pretrained controls; an epoch-budget comparison; and dropout-free training through the terminal training phase. Original protocols remain. Appendix D's exact budget allocation and the full 100-client setup are underspecified locally.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained codebook, threshold, imbalance, and 50-client analyses, v4 investigates heterogeneity severity, training-budget effects, Deep Ensembles versus MC Dropout, neural collapse, and convergence after codebook extensions. Appendices C–H substantially broaden the questions tested.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly reports predictive-uncertainty estimation using five ensembles alongside MC Dropout. The existing 20-pass dropout evaluation remains unchanged. Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the ensemble count is not evidence of repeated full-experiment trials.

E6.justification: Retained tables and plots preserve their results, while v4 adds extensive result entries. For example, Table 4 reports UEFL versus FedCR accuracies of 98.29 versus 97.47 on EMNIST-L and 63.37 versus 62.96 on CIFAR100 under 100 clients. V4 also removes v3's incorrectly D3-attributed MNIST improvement percentages.

T1.justification: V3 contains method and metric equations but no generalization theorems. V4 adds partition definitions, boundedness/Lipschitz assumptions, two IID generalization bounds attributed to Liu et al., and two non-IID bounds involving client/global KL divergence in Appendices A–B. Proofs of the new federated bounds are not supplied.

C1.justification: The central UEFL contributions and headline improvement ranges remain. V4 removes the introduction's unconditional guarantee of termination within a few iterations and changes the evaluation scope from six datasets to various datasets. These are limited qualifications and scope updates.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive explanations involving noise robustness, reduced dimensionality, and reduced client/global divergence. It also attributes poor CIFAR100 performance to severe heterogeneity, discusses ensemble cost and dropout-related overfitting, and identifies diminishing accuracy/uncertainty benefits from further extensions. These substantially expand v3's interpretation of mechanisms and practical boundaries.

D1.justification: V4 adds a source-code access URL, explicitly describes averaging codewords across their participating clients, specifies a five-iteration maximum, and documents codebook-growth sequences and the model size used for timing. Core hardware, backbones, dropout settings, and dataset-specific thresholds were already disclosed in v3.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting FedCR and neural-collapse comparisons, plus several background/reference entries. It develops the already cited Liu et al. work into an explicit theoretical foundation. The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V4 makes targeted edits to the abstract, contribution statements, methodology, metrics, and performance discussion; distinguishes codebook-size notation; and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Original appendices are relabeled behind the new material.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, redraws Figures 1–2, and replaces the main multidomain table with an aggregate summary while retaining its detailed version in Appendix C. It adds several tables and convergence figures and expands the codeword-count table with a growth column.

improvement.justification: The added heterogeneity controls and estimator comparison strengthen empirical support, while implementation disclosures and a code-access pointer aid reproducibility. Removing the misattributed MNIST percentages and unconditional termination guarantee also improves precision. These gains are tempered by unproved federated bounds and Appendix G's claimed 256-codeword maximum despite documented 512-codeword ablations, yielding a limited net improvement.
